headline: Margins expand, profits surge; cash drawn by buybacks
summary_short: Graco's Q2 2026 net sales rose 3.3% y/y to $590.6M as diluted EPS climbed 14.5% to $0.87 ($0.91 adjusted), helped by $9M of net tariff refunds and a ~1pp gross-margin gain; the company guided Q3 2026 total sales to $580M-$600M, excluding its pending $447M Valco Melton acquisition.
summary_long: Operating margin expanded to 29.6% (from 27.5% y/y) as $9M of net tariff refunds and lower opex offset a 1% organic sales decline from Industrial finishing-system timing; acquisitions added 3 points and FX 1 point to the 3.3% y/y sales growth. Contractor operating earnings rose 21% y/y on broad Americas strength and tariff refunds; Industrial earnings rose modestly as flat margins met acquisition-driven volume. Cash fell to $507.6M (from $712.2M q/q) after $315M of buybacks and $48M of quarterly dividends; equity fell 8% q/q for the same reason. Graco guided Q3 2026 sales to $580M-$600M, excluding the pending $447M Valco Melton deal (closing Q3), and outlined a low-single-digit 2026 organic sales outlook.

drivers.explanation: 3 percentage points of growth came from acquired operations and 1 point from favorable currency, partially offset by a 1-point organic decline tied to the timing of Industrial finishing-system and other project sales.
Gross margin rose about 1pp for the quarter as price realization and $9M of net tariff refunds more than offset lower margin rates from acquired operations.
Adjusted operating earnings rose 11% on the higher gross margin plus lower operating expenses, including reduced stock compensation and marketing/product-development spending.
Tracked operating-earnings growth plus $6M higher other non-operating income (lower FX losses on foreign-currency net assets), partly offset by a higher 20.1% effective tax rate (vs 19.3% y/y).
Grew faster than net earnings on a 1.7% y/y reduction in diluted share count from continued buybacks ($315M repurchased this quarter).
Cash fell $205M q/q as $315M of share buybacks and $48M of dividends this quarter outpaced operating cash flow, only partly offset by $4.9M of stock issuance proceeds.

Fell 8% q/q as $315M of share buybacks depleted retained earnings and paid-in capital faster than net income and translation gains added to them; still up modestly y/y on twelve months of profit accretion outpacing buybacks.

MD&A frames the quarter as broad-based margin expansion (tariff refunds, price realization, lower opex) funding continued buybacks, alongside a definitive $447M agreement to acquire Valco Melton (adhesive dispensing/QA systems), expected to close in Q3 2026.
